verses.sanskrit:
भीम उवाच।
              ाण्डवो भीमसेनोऽहं धर्मराजादनन्तरः ।
              विशालां बदरीं प्राप्तो भ्रातृभिः सह राक्षसाः ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhima said: I am Bhimasena, the son of Pandu. I am next in birth to Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira). O Rakshasas, I had come with my brother to the great Badari.

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यत्तत्र पाञ्चाली सौगन्धिकमनुत्तमम् । अनिलोढमितो नूनं सा बहूनि परीप्सति ॥२॥
verses.english: There did the Panchala princess see an excellent Sugandhika (lotus), which was certainly carried there by wind from this place. She desired to possess more of that kind lotus.

verses.sanskrit: तस्या मामनवद्याङ्ग्या धर्मपत्न्याः प्रिये स्थितम् । पुष्पाहारमिह प्राप्तं निबोधत निशाचराः ॥ ३॥
verses.english: There did the Panchala princess see an excellent Sugandhika (lotus), which was certainly carried there by wind from this place. She desired to possess more of that kind lotus.

verses.sanskrit:
राक्षसा ऊचुः।
              आक्रीडोऽयं कुबेरस्य दयितः पुरुषर्षभ ।
              नेह शक्यं मनुष्येण विहर्तुं मर्त्यधर्मणा ॥४॥
verses.english: The Rakshasas said : O foremost of men, this place is the favourite play-ground of Kubera. Men subject to the laws of earth cannot sport here.

verses.sanskrit: देवर्षयस्तथा यक्षा देवाश्चात्र वृकोदर । आमन्त्र्य यक्षप्रवरं पिबन्ति रमयन्ति च । गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव विहरन्त्यत्र पाण्डव ॥५॥
verses.english: O Vrikodara, the celestials Rishis, the Yakshas and the celestials, after taking permission of the Yaksha chief, drink the water of this lake and sport here. O Pandava, the Gandharvas and the Apsaras (also) sport here.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यायेनेह यः कश्चिदवमन्य धनेश्वरम् । विहर्तुमिच्छेद्दुर्वृत्तः स विनश्येन्न संशयः ॥६॥
verses.english: That wicked person, who without heeding the lord of wealth (Kubera), unlawfully tries to sport here, certainly meets with destruction.

verses.sanskrit: तमनादृत्य पद्मानि जिहीर्षसि बलादृतः । धर्मराजस्य चात्मानं ब्रवीषि भ्रातरं कथम् ॥७॥
verses.english: Without heeding him (Kubera), you intend to take away the lotuses from this place by main force, why then do you say that you are the brother of Dharmaraja?

verses.sanskrit: आमन्त्र्य यक्षराजं वै ततः पिब हरस्व च । नातोऽन्यथा त्वया शक्यं किंचित्पुष्करमीक्षितुम्॥८॥
verses.english: First take the permission of the king of the Yakshas and then drink (the water of this lake) and take away (the lotuses) If you do not act thus, you will not be able even to look at these flowers.

verses.sanskrit:
भीमसेन उवाच।
              राक्षसास्तं न पश्यामि धनेश्वरमिहान्तिके । दृष्टापि च महाराजं नाहं याचितुमुत्सहे ॥९॥
verses.english: Bhimasena said: Rakshasas, I do not see the lord of wealth here. Even if I see that great king, I shall not pray (for the flowers) to him,

verses.sanskrit: न हि याचन्ति राजान एष धर्मः सनातनः । न चाहं हातुमिच्छामि क्षात्रधर्मं कथंचन ॥१०॥
verses.english: The Kshatriyas never beg; this is the eternal Dharma. I never wish to forsake the duties of a Kshatriya.

verses.sanskrit: इयं च नलिनी रम्या जाता पर्वतनिर्झरे । नेयं भवनमासाद्य कुबेरस्य महात्मनः ॥११॥
verses.english: The lotus-lake has sprung up on the mountain breast. It has not been made in the abode of the illustrious Kubera.

verses.sanskrit: तुल्या हि सर्वभूतानामियं वैश्रवणस्य च। एवं गतेषु द्रव्येषु कः कं याचितुमर्हति ॥१२॥
verses.english: (Therefore) it belongs to every body equally with Vaisravana (Kubera). In such things, who should beg to others?

verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच ।
              इत्युक्त्वा राक्षसान्सर्वान्भीमसेनो ह्यमर्षणः । व्यगाहत महाबाहुर्नलिनीं तां महाबलः ॥१३॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Having said this to all the Rakshasas, the mighty-armed and exceedingly unforbearing and greatly strong Bhimasena plunged into the lake.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स राक्षसैर्वाचा प्रतिषिद्धः प्रतापवान् । मा मैवमिति सक्रोधैर्भर्त्सयद्भिः समन्ततः ॥१४॥
verses.english: Thereupon that powerful hero was forbidden by the Rakshasas, saying “Don't do it” and from all sides they began to abuse him in anger.

verses.sanskrit: कदर्थीकृत्य तु स तान्राक्षसान्भीमविक्रमः । व्यगाहत महातेःस्ते तं सर्वे न्यवारयन् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Not heeding them at all, that greatly powerful one plunged (into the lake). But they (the Rakshasas) prepared themselves to oppose him.

verses.sanskrit: गृह्णीत प्रध्नीत विकर्ततेमं पचाम खादाम च भीमसेनम् । क्रुद्धा ब्रुवन्तोऽभिययुर्द्रुतं ते शस्त्राणि चोद्यम्य विवृततनेत्राः ॥१६॥
verses.english: With rolling eyes, they upraised their arms and rushed in anger at Bhimasena, crying "Seize him" "Bind him," "Cut him down" "Look to Bhima and eat him up."

verses.sanskrit: ततः स गुर्वीं यमदण्डकल्पां महागदां काञ्चनपट्टनद्धाम् । प्रगृह्य तानभ्यपतत्तरस्वी ततोऽब्रवीत्तिष्ठत तिष्ठतेति ॥१७॥
verses.english: Thereupon that greatly powerful hero, taking up his huge and mighty mace inlaid with gold which resembled the mace of Yama himself, turned towards those (Rakshasas) and exclaimed, "Stay," "Stay".

verses.sanskrit: ते तं तदा तोभरपट्टिशाद्यैर्व्याविद्धशस्त्रैः सहसा निपेतुः । जिघांसवः क्रोधवशाः सुभीमा भीमं समन्तात् परिववुरुग्राः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Thereupon they rushed upon him with great force upraising their lances, axes and other weapons. Desiring to kill Bhima, those dreadful and fearful Krodhavasas surrounded hiin on all sides.

verses.sanskrit: घातेन कुन्त्यां बलवान् सुजातः शूरस्तरस्वी द्विषतां निहन्ता । सत्ये च धर्मे च रतः सदैव पराक्रमे शत्रुभिरप्रधृष्यः ॥१९॥
verses.english: But that mighty hero was begotten by Vayu in the womb of Kunti. He was heroic and courageous; that slayer of foes was ever devoted to virtue and truth. He was incapable of being vanquished by any enemy through prowess.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां स मार्गान् विविधान् महात्मा विहन्य शस्त्राणि च शात्रवाणाम् । यथा प्रवीरान्निजघान भीमः परं शतं पुष्करिणीसमीपे ॥२०॥
verses.english: Therefore on the banks of that lake he defeated the foes and broke their arms. He kiiled more than one hundred, beginning from the foremost.

verses.sanskrit: ते तस्य वीर्यं च बलं च दृष्ट्वा विद्याबलं बाहुबलं तथैव । अशक्नुवन्तः सहितं समन्ताद्द्रुतं प्रवीराः सहसा निवृत्ताः ॥२१॥
verses.english: Seeing his prowess, strength and also the might of his arms, those foremost of heroes, being unable to withstand (his attack), began suddenly to fly in all directions.
verses.bhavadeepa: विहन्य विनाश्य । ’वा ल्यपि’ इत्यनुनासिकालोपपक्षे इदं रूपम् ॥२०॥

verses.sanskrit: विदीर्यमाणास्तत एव हन्तुमाकाशमास्थाय विमूढसंज्ञाः । कैलासशृङ्गाण्यभिदुद्रुवुस्ते भीमार्दिताः क्रोधवशाः प्रभग्नाः॥२२॥
verses.english: Beaten and pierced by Bhimasena, those Krodhavasas left the field of battle and confusedly and hurriedly fled towards Kailasha mountain through the sky.

verses.sanskrit: स शक्रवद्दानवदैत्यसङ्घान् विक्रम्य जित्वा च रणेऽरिसङ्घान् । विगाह्य तां पुष्करिणीं जितारिः कामाय जग्राह ततोऽम्बुजानि ॥२३॥
verses.english: Having thus vanquished those Rakshasas by his prowess, as Indra did the armies of the Daityas and the Danavas, he again plunged into the lake and began to gather the lotuses with the object of accomplishing his purpose.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स पीत्वाऽमृतकल्पमम्भो भूयो बभूवोत्तमवीर्यतेजाः । उत्पाट्य जग्राह च सोऽम्बुजानि सौगन्धिकान्युत्तमगन्धवन्ति ॥२४॥
verses.english: When he drank the water (of the lake) which was like ambrosia, his energy and strength were again fully restored; he then plucked and gathered the golden lotuses of excellent fragrance.
verses.bhavadeepa: विक्रम्य जित्वा च अभिभूय वशीकृक्त्य चेत्यर्थः ॥२३॥

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु ते क्रोधवशाः समेत्य धनेश्वरं भीमबलप्रणुन्नाः । भीमस्य वीर्यं च बलं च सङ्ख्ये यथावदाचख्युरतीव भीताः ॥२५॥
verses.english: (In the mean while) the Krodhavasas, being driven by the prowess of Bhima and greatly terrified, went to the lord of wealth (Kubera) and informed him of Bhima's prowess and strength.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां वचस्तत्तु निशम्य देवः प्रहस्य रक्षांसि ततोऽभ्युवाच । गृह्णातु भीमो जलजानि कामात् कृष्णानिमित्तं विदितं ममैतत् ॥२६॥
verses.english: Having heard their words, the deity (Kubera) smiled and then said, 'Let Bhima take for Krishna (Draupadi) as many lotuses as he likes. This is already known to me."

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽभ्यनुज्ञाप्य धनेश्वरं ते जग्मुः कुरूणां प्रवरं विरोषाः। भीमं च तस्यां ददृशुर्नलिन्यां यथोपजोषं विहरन्तमेकम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: Thereupon taking the permission of the lord of wealth (Kubera) and giving up their anger, those (Rakshasas) went (back) to that foremost of the Kurus (Bhima); and they saw Bhima alone sporting in delight in that lotus-lake.
